emily: Kicking off a short thread to finalize the benchmark narrative for launch. Need 1 hero stat + 2 supporting visuals (price-vs-speed scatter + unit-econ waterfall). Keep copy audience-specific (PLG vs enterprise).
carter: Hero stat should be p95 for chat and cost-per-1k for batch. Example copy: "Observed p95 < 55ms on standard chat prompt; $0.80 / 1k tokens for embeddings (hosted)". Use "observed" in all public copy.
diego: Visuals: scatter where x=median latency (ms), y=cost/1k (USD), shapes for deployment mode. Add iso-contours for equal tradeoff. Waterfall to show savings from batching, caching, quantization. Include small appendix table with sample prompts and seq lengths.
harper: Webinar plan: 22 minutes. 5m framing, 10m chart walkthrough + live routing demo, 5m quick wins, 2m CTA. Routing CTA mapping: latency -> SDR fast-track, cost -> self-serve nurture. Landing form fields: workload, priority, monthly tokens.
emily: Copy hooks to A/B test: 1) "Predictable tails, measurable savings" 2) "Fast where you need it, cheaper where it counts" 3) "Benchmark-backed inference decisions". My pick for PLG is 2, enterprise 1.
carter: Benchbot, paste latest run summary please.
benchbot: automated: latest-run-1768504000.csv attached. summary: median(chat)=10.5ms, p95(chat)=51ms, host_cost/1k=$0.87, dedicated reduces p95 by ~29% avg. prefix cache saved ~33% tokens on multi-turn. sample size=48k requests.
diego: We'll need methodology footnote for any "99.9% under X ms" claims. Also include a reproducibility appendix in the gated download.
harper: Social caption ideas: short and punchy. Examples: "Speed you can plan for. Costs you can measure. See our benchmark." and "Where should you trade latency for price? We measured it." Add CTA to webinar + gated CSV.
emily: Action items: diego -> generate CSV + iso-contour script by Tue, carter -> 4 caption variants + 3 email subjects by Mon EOD, harper -> landing copy + routing flows, benchbot -> attach reproducibility notes. We'll iterate after first impressions. :rocket:
file_name_note: thread contains short Slack-style messages; timestamps are plausible and in order
